title: Facilitating Cerebral Organoid Culture via Lateral Soft Light Illumination
protocol: Collect 3 mL of peripheral blood by venipuncture with informed consent from volunteers and patients.
Isolate peripheral blood mononuclear cells according to the Ficoll-Paque method.
Establish iPSCs according to the protocol of the Sendai Reprogramming Kit.
Culture the iPSCs with mTeSR1 medium in 35 mm Petri dishes covered with Matrigel.
Change the medium every day.
Maintain iPSC growth density below 75%.
Digest the cells with PSC dissociation solution.
Subculture the cells at a ratio of 1:5 every 3-5 days.
Remove the mTeSR1 medium from the iPSCs using a pipette.
Wash the iPSCs twice with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Add 300 μL of cell detachment solution to digest the iPSCs into single cells for 3-4 min at 37 °C.
Resuspend the cells in 2 mL of EB-formation medium containing Y-27632 (final concentration, 10 µM).
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 300 x g (room temperature).
Pretreat the specialized 24-well plate with anti-adherence rinsing solution (500 μL/well) for 5 min.
Remove the anti-adherence rinsing solution and rinse each well with 2 mL of EB-formation medium.
Add the cells to the specialized 24-well plates at a density of 3 x 10^6 cells/well.
Centrifuge the plate at 100 x g for 2 min at room temperature.
Uniformly distribute the cells in each chamber at the bottom of the plate.
Incubate the samples at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h if centrifugation was performed.
Incubate the samples at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 36 h if no centrifugation was used.
Install a row of LED white lights on the edge of an acrylic plate so that light enters from the side.
Prepare a new 6-well low adhesion plate.
Add 2 mL of EB-formation medium to each well in the prepared plate.
Remove EBs together with the medium using a 1000 µL wide-bore pipette tip.
Transfer EBs to the 6-well low adhesion plate (~100 EBs/well).
Replace with fresh EB-formation medium every day.
Use secondary flow to gather EBs to the center and change the medium.
Aspirate old medium by pipetting to the edge of the well slowly.
Add fresh medium to resuspend the EBs.
Fix EBs in 4% paraformaldehyde at 4 °C for 30 min.
Wash EBs in 1x PBS three times, each for 10 min.
Transfer EBs to room temperature PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 and 3% BSA for 2 h.
Wash EBs in PBS three times, each for 10 min.
Dilute the OCT4 primary antibody with 1 mL of 1x PBS containing 1% BSA at a ratio of 1:200.
Add the diluted OCT4 primary antibody to the EBs for incubation at 4 °C overnight.
Wash the EBs in PBS 3 times, each time for 10 minutes.
Dilute the respective secondary antibody with 1x PBS at a ratio of 1:500.
Add 1 mL of diluted secondary antibody to the EBs and incubate at room temperature for 2 hours.
Wash the cells in 1x PBS 3 times, each time for 10 minutes.
Remove the PBS and add 2 mL of 1x PBS solution containing 1 µg/mL DAPI.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Wash the EBs in PBS 3 times, each time for 10 minutes.
Move the EB containing a small amount of liquid onto the slide.
Seal the slide with a cover glass coated with commercially available petroleum jelly on the edge.
Observe and collect the image under the fluorescence confocal microscope.
Prepare a new 6-well plate with low adhesion.
Add 3 mL of Neural induction medium to each well in the 6-well plate.
Transfer the EBs to the 6-well plate containing Neural induction medium (~100 EBs/well).
Add as little as possible of the original medium to the new well.
Place the membrane matrix in a 4 °C refrigerator for 60 min in advance to dissolve.
Calculate the amount of required matrix in advance.
Transfer a small amount of EBs to a 60 mm dish containing fresh expansion medium each time.
Reduce the number of EBs to make it easier to remove a single EB.
Use a new 6-well low adhesion plate.
Suck a single EB with approximately 10 µL medium using a 200 µL wide-bore pipette tip.
Add the EB to the bottom of the 6-well plate to form droplets.
Place five droplets per well.
Adjust the range of the pipette gun to 50 µL and suck an EB.
Refer to the operation instructions for forming droplets.
Quickly touch the well bottom with the pipette tip containing approximately 10 µL liquid to form a droplet.
Add 15 µL of membrane matrix to each drop containing EB.
Mix the membrane matrix quickly with the EB.
Embed the EB ball in the center of the droplet.
Place the 6-well plate into a 37 °C incubator for 30 min.
Solidify the membrane matrix droplets containing EBs.
Add 3 mL of expansion medium to each well.
Gently blow up the matrix-embedded EBs to suspend them.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Remove the original medium gently.
Add 3 mL of maturation medium to each well.
Place the organoid plate on a horizontal shaker in a 37 °C incubator.
Rotate the culture horizontally.
Set the shaker speed according to the manufacturer's specifications for RCF of 0.11808 x g.
Change the fresh Maturation medium every 2-3 days.
Fix the organoids in 4% paraformaldehyde at 4 °C for 16 hours.
Wash the organoids three times with 1x PBS for 10 minutes each time.
Immerse the organoids in 30% sucrose at 4 °C overnight.
Embed the organoids in 10%/7.5% gelatine/sucrose at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Quickly transfer the embedded organoids to an embedding mold.
Prepare a dry ice/ethanol slurry and place the organoid samples into it for quick freezing.
Store frozen samples in a -80 °C freezer.
Make frozen sections with a thickness of 20 μm when required.
Label apical progenitor cells using the PAX6 antibody.
Label neuronal cells using the TUJ1 antibody.
Stain nuclear DNA using DAPI.
